misconception.text: The pressure in a liquid is the same at every depth.

correction.text: It grows with depth, so the pressure at the bottom of a container is greater than at the top.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: An object floats or sinks according to whether it is lighter or heavier than the same volume of water.

correction.text: It floats or sinks according to its density compared with the fluid, not its weight compared with the fluid.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

stem.text: Poiseuille's law says that the volume flow rate of a fluid through a tube varies as

explanation.text: The flow rate varies as the fourth power of the radius, so a tube twice as wide carries sixteen times the flow.

stem.text: A small object falling through a viscous fluid eventually reaches a constant speed because

options.text: the buoyant force balances its weight
the viscous drag balances the weight less buoyancy

explanation.text: At the terminal speed the net force is zero, so the upward viscous drag balances the downward weight less the buoyant force.

stem.text: Pascal's principle states that a change of pressure in an enclosed fluid is

options.text: transmitted undiminished to every part of the fluid
halved at each metre of depth

explanation.text: The pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions, which is what makes the hydraulic press work.

stem.text: A body floats in water when

options.text: its weight equals the weight of the water displaced
its density is greater than that of water
its volume equals the volume of water displaced

explanation.text: By Archimedes' principle a floating body displaces its own weight of water, so the upthrust equals its weight.
